page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the cost-optimized E2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model that provides a fractional, one-half physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports hardware-assisted virtualization, Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and hyper-threading.

Benchmark data highlights a significant performance asymmetry due to the shared-core architecture. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2642.19. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 2642.78, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem performance is constrained, with read-only large block memory bandwidth at 6.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 4.83 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 661.0 and 682.0, respectively, reflect the resource-constrained nature of the shared-core allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers a highly economical entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute resources. The shared-core model allows for low-cost baseline operations, making it suitable for lightweight applications, development environments, small-scale web serving, and basic background tasks. However, the poor memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling make it unsuitable for database operations, heavy multi-threaded processing, or memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include microservices, small utility scripts, and low-traffic static web servers.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance within the E2 family, designed for budget-conscious, low-intensity workloads. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast: while single-core CPU performance is relatively strong, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are highly constrained, placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. This resource profile makes the e2-medium highly cost-efficient for lightweight, non-continuous tasks but unsuitable for demanding applications. It is best utilized for development environments, microservices, low-traffic static web serving, and basic administrative scripting.
